en.intro: There are now more than a dozen ways to talk instead of type on a Mac. They split on two questions: where your voice is transcribed, and what you pay. This page puts them in one table, then says who each one suits.

sections.heading: Cloud or local is the first choice
body: [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative), [Typeless](typeless-alternative), [Aqua Voice](aqua-voice-alternative) and [Willow Voice](willow-voice-alternative) send your audio to their servers. That buys them large models and AI rewriting, and it is why they meter words and charge monthly. They also stop working when the connection does.

TypeAloud, [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative), [MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative) and the free tiers of [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative) and [Spokenly](spokenly-alternative) run a speech model on your Mac. Nothing is uploaded, there is no quota, and they work offline. The trade-off is a one-time model download and wanting an Apple Silicon Mac.

sections.heading: Then: an input method, or a transcription tool?
body: Some apps behave like a keyboard: hold a key, speak, and the text appears where you were typing. TypeAloud, Wispr Flow, Typeless, Superwhisper, VoiceInk and Spokenly work this way.
MacWhisper is built around recordings. It is excellent at turning an interview or a meeting into a transcript, and its dictation window is a Pro extra rather than the centre of the app.

sections.heading: Prices and head-to-heads
body: For the subscription details, see [Wispr Flow pricing](wispr-flow-pricing) and [Typeless pricing](typeless-pricing). If you are choosing between two of them, there are direct comparisons of [Wispr Flow and Typeless](wispr-flow-vs-typeless), [Wispr Flow and Superwhisper](wispr-flow-vs-superwhisper), and [Superwhisper and MacWhisper](superwhisper-vs-macwhisper).

sections.heading: By use case
body: Looking for something specific: [free dictation with no word limit](free-dictation-mac), [open-source dictation](open-source-dictation-mac), [voice input for Claude Code and Cursor](voice-coding), or [an answer to Whisper's trouble with mixed Chinese and English](whisper-chinese-english).

sections.heading: Where TypeAloud fits
body: TypeAloud is the free, open-source option for dictating straight into any Mac app. Its local model, [Qwen3-ASR](qwen3-asr-mac), detects the spoken language itself, so a sentence that switches between Chinese and English needs no setting change. It does not rewrite what you say, and it has no phone app.

faq.q: What is the best free dictation app for Mac?
faq.a: If you want unlimited dictation with no account, pick an app that runs locally. TypeAloud is free and open source; Superwhisper and Spokenly have free local tiers; Apple Dictation is built in but stops after a pause.

faq.q: Which Mac dictation apps work offline?
faq.a: The local ones: TypeAloud, VoiceInk, MacWhisper, and Superwhisper or Spokenly with a local model. Cloud apps such as Wispr Flow, Typeless, Aqua Voice and Willow Voice need a connection.

faq.q: Which one is best for Chinese?
faq.a: Look for a model trained heavily on Chinese. TypeAloud uses Qwen3-ASR, which handles Chinese and mixed Chinese–English speech. Whisper-based apps tend to struggle when a sentence switches language.

faq.q: Which Macs can run it?
faq.a: Apple Silicon is recommended for local dictation. The recommended model is a one-time download of about 1 GB.

en.intro: Wispr Flow and Typeless are the two best-known AI dictation apps. Both send your voice to the cloud, tidy it into writing and drop it at your cursor. They cost the same per year. The differences are in monthly pricing, extras and platforms.

sections.heading: Same idea, different emphasis
body: Wispr Flow leans towards work and teams: a meeting Notetaker, shared dictionaries and snippets, and higher tiers with SSO and HIPAA enforcement. Typeless leans into editing: it turns rambling speech into tidy prose, translates, has an Ask anything feature and a whisper mode for quiet rooms. Typeless also runs on Linux.

sections.heading: Price: equal yearly, very different monthly
body: Billed yearly, both Pro plans come to $144. Month to month, Wispr Flow is $15 and Typeless is $30, so a year of monthly billing costs $180 against $360. If you will not commit to a year, Wispr Flow costs half as much. Details: [Wispr Flow pricing](wispr-flow-pricing), [Typeless pricing](typeless-pricing).

sections.heading: What both have in common
body: Both need a connection, both send your audio to their servers, and both meter the free plan for that reason. If you want dictation that stays on your Mac and costs nothing, [TypeAloud](best-dictation-apps-mac) is the third option. It writes what you said rather than rewriting it.

faq.q: Which is cheaper, Wispr Flow or Typeless?
faq.a: Billed yearly they cost the same, $12 a month. Month to month, Wispr Flow is $15 and Typeless is $30.

faq.q: Do Wispr Flow or Typeless work offline?
faq.a: No. Both transcribe in the cloud. For offline dictation you need a local app; see [offline dictation for Mac](offline-dictation-mac).

faq.q: Which is better for Chinese?
faq.a: Both list over 100 languages. If you mix Chinese and English in the same sentence, TypeAloud's local Qwen3-ASR model [is built for that](chinese-english-dictation).

faq.q: Is there a free alternative to both?
faq.a: Yes. TypeAloud is free, open source and local. See how it compares with [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative) and [Typeless](typeless-alternative).

body: Every Wispr Flow dictation goes to its servers. Superwhisper's free plan runs Whisper on your Mac with no word limit, and Pro adds both larger local models and cloud models. If you want dictation that works on a plane, only Superwhisper of the two does it.

sections.heading: If you want local and simple

faq.q: Does Superwhisper work offline?

faq.q: Which is easier to set up?

heading: Superwhisper or MacWhisper?
They answer different questions.
en.intro: The names are similar and both run Whisper on your Mac, so they get compared a lot. In practice Superwhisper is for speaking into the app you are using, and MacWhisper is for turning recordings into transcripts. Pick by which of those you do most.

sections.heading: Dictation versus transcription
body: Superwhisper starts from a shortcut: press it in any text field, speak, press again, and the text is pasted where you were. Its modes can rewrite what you said into an email or message.

MacWhisper starts from a file: drop in an interview, lecture or meeting recording and get a transcript with speakers labelled, then export it as subtitles or a document. Its dictation feature, Global, is part of Pro and works through its own floating window.

sections.heading: Which to pick
body: If you write by voice every day, Superwhisper. If you transcribe recordings, MacWhisper; its €64 one-time Pro is good value for that. Plenty of people use both.

sections.heading: A free dictation option
body: For the dictation half, TypeAloud is free and open source, runs locally, and needs no configuration: hold Ctrl+Shift, speak, release. Its Qwen3-ASR model handles [mixed Chinese and English](chinese-english-dictation). See [TypeAloud vs Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative) and [TypeAloud vs MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative).

faq.q: Is MacWhisper a dictation app?
faq.a: Mainly it is a transcription app for files and meetings. Dictation is available in Pro through a floating window.

faq.q: Can Superwhisper transcribe audio files?
faq.a: Yes, on Pro. MacWhisper has more for recordings: batch processing, speaker labels and subtitle export.

faq.q: Which is cheaper?
faq.a: MacWhisper Pro is a one-time €64. Superwhisper Pro is $84.99 a year or $249.99 once. Both have free versions.

sections.heading: Why the word cap disappears
body: Wispr Flow sends each recording to its servers, and every dictated word costs it compute. That is what [the weekly cap and the Pro plan](wispr-flow-pricing) pay for.

TypeAloud downloads a speech model once (Qwen3-ASR 0.6B, about 1 GB) and runs it on your Mac. After that, dictating 200 words or 20,000 words in a week costs nobody anything, so there is [no quota to enforce](free-dictation-mac).

sections.heading: The same hold, speak, release habit
body: Hold Ctrl+Shift in whatever app you are writing in, speak, and release. The text lands at your cursor: in your editor, your terminal, Slack, a browser field. Escape cancels a recording.
Finished transcripts are kept in History on your device. If a transcription fails and the audio was saved, you can retry it.

sections.heading: Where Wispr Flow is the better choice
body: Wispr Flow rewrites what you say: it drops filler words, fixes self-corrections and adjusts tone to the app you are in. TypeAloud gives you an accurate transcript of what you said and leaves the wording to you.
Wispr Flow also has iPhone and Android apps and team plans. TypeAloud is a desktop app, tested mainly on macOS. If you dictate on your phone or need shared team dictionaries, Wispr Flow fits better.

faq.q: Is TypeAloud really free?
faq.a: Yes. Local transcription needs no account, API key or subscription, and there is no word limit. Cloud transcription is optional and uses your own Groq or OpenAI key, which those providers may charge for.

faq.q: Does my audio leave my Mac?
faq.a: Not in local mode. The model runs on your device and transcripts are saved there. Audio is only uploaded if you choose a cloud engine with your own API key.

faq.q: Which Macs can run it?
faq.a: Apple Silicon is recommended for local dictation. The recommended model is a one-time download of about 1 GB.

faq.q: Is there a Windows version?
faq.a: There are Windows and Linux builds, but they are experimental. macOS is the platform TypeAloud is tested on.

faq.q: Does Wispr Flow work offline?
faq.a: No. Wispr Flow transcribes on its servers, so it needs an internet connection. TypeAloud's local mode works with no connection after the model download; see [offline dictation for Mac](offline-dictation-mac).

faq.q: How much is Wispr Flow Pro?

faq.q: Is Wispr Flow better than Typeless?

Plenty of people use both: MacWhisper for files, and a dictation app for everyday writing.

For exact identifiers, file paths and flags, typing is still quicker. Speak the intent, type the camelCase.

body: TypeAloud runs Q8_0 builds of Qwen3-ASR through llama.cpp with Metal on Apple Silicon. A worker is warmed while you speak, so most of the load time overlaps your sentence. On Windows and Linux the same models run on the CPU, with optional Vulkan on Windows; those builds are experimental.
The timings above exclude recording and insertion, and come from the TypeAloud maintainer's measurements on an M4.

sections.heading: Long recordings
body: Qwen3-ASR works best on clips of a minute or less, so TypeAloud cuts long dictation at natural pauses into pieces of 20 to 75 seconds and transcribes each while you keep talking. When you release, the pieces are joined, without stray spaces between Chinese characters, and inserted once.

sections.heading: Which size to use
body: Start with 0.6B. It is fast on any Apple Silicon Mac. TypeAloud records how quickly your Mac transcribes, and once it has enough samples it suggests 1.7B if a 15-second sentence would still come back within about 1.5 seconds. Whether 1.7B is more accurate on everyday dictation has not been measured, so treat it as an option, not an upgrade.

sections.heading: No language setting
body: Qwen3-ASR takes no language parameter; it detects the language from the audio. That is why [mixed Chinese and English](chinese-english-dictation) works without switching anything, and why it is a common answer to [Whisper's trouble with mixed speech](whisper-chinese-english).

en.title: Whisper and mixed Chinese–English speech: why it fails and what works — TypeAloud
en.description: Whisper decodes each window in one language, so sentences that switch between Chinese and English come out wrong. Workarounds, and models built for mixed speech.
heading: Why Whisper garbles
mixed Chinese and English.
en.intro: Say "帮我 review 一下这个 pull request" to a Whisper-based dictation app and you may get the English words spelled out in Chinese characters, dropped, or the whole sentence turned into English. This page explains why, what you can try, and which models handle it properly.

sections.heading: One language per window
body: Whisper processes audio in 30-second windows. For each window it first picks a language, either the one you set or the one it detects, and then writes the whole window in that language. A sentence that switches languages halfway gets forced into one of them.

Its vocabulary is shared across languages and most of its training audio is in a single language, so switching mid-sentence is exactly the case it saw least. Research on Whisper and code-switching describes errors clustering at the switch points.

sections.heading: Workarounds if you stay with Whisper
body: Set the language to Chinese rather than letting it detect, so short English words do not flip the whole window into English.

Use the initial prompt. A prompt written in Simplified Chinese that includes the English terms you use, such as product names, nudges Whisper to keep them in Latin letters and to write Simplified rather than Traditional characters.
Fine-tuning on mixed Chinese–English data helps most. Published work using small adapters on top of Whisper reports clear gains on mixed speech, but that is a research project, not a setting.

sections.heading: Use a model trained for it
body: Newer speech models trained heavily on Chinese handle switching natively. Qwen3-ASR has no language parameter at all: it works out the language from the audio as it goes. [TypeAloud runs Qwen3-ASR on your Mac](qwen3-asr-mac) as a dictation app, so a mixed sentence comes out as you said it. More on [mixed Chinese–English dictation](chinese-english-dictation).

faq.q: Does Whisper support Chinese?
faq.a: Yes. It transcribes Mandarin well when you speak only Chinese. The problem is switching languages within a sentence.

faq.q: Why does Whisper output Traditional Chinese?
faq.a: Its training data mixes Simplified and Traditional text. An initial prompt written in Simplified Chinese usually steers it to Simplified.

faq.q: Which dictation apps use Whisper?
faq.a: Many local Mac apps, including [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative), [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative) and [MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative), offer Whisper models.

faq.q: Is there a free app that handles mixed speech?
faq.a: TypeAloud is free and open source, and uses Qwen3-ASR locally on your Mac.

zh.title: Whisper 中英混合识别不准？原因、解决办法和替代模型 — TypeAloud
zh.description: Whisper 每个窗口只按一种语言解码，中英夹杂的句子就容易出错，还常输出繁体。原因、可以试的办法，以及专门处理中英混说的模型。
heading: Whisper 为什么
听不准中英混说。
zh.intro: 对着基于 Whisper 的听写应用说"帮我 review 一下这个 pull request"，你可能会得到被写成汉字音译的英文、被吞掉的英文，或者整句被翻成英文。这一页讲清楚原因、能试的办法，以及哪些模型能正确处理。

sections.heading: 一个窗口，一种语言
body: Whisper 按 30 秒的窗口处理音频。每个窗口先定一种语言，要么是你设置的，要么是它检测出来的，然后整个窗口都按这种语言写。半句中文半句英文的话，会被强行写成其中一种。
它的词表是所有语言共用的，训练音频大多是单一语言，所以句中切换语言正是它见得最少的情况。关于 Whisper 语码转换的研究也发现，错误集中出现在语言切换的位置。

sections.heading: 继续用 Whisper 的话可以试试
body: 把语言设成中文，不要让它自动检测，这样几个英文单词不会把整个窗口带成英文。
利用 initial prompt。写一段简体中文的提示，把你常用的英文词（比如产品名）放进去，可以让 Whisper 保留英文拼写，并输出简体而不是繁体。
效果最好的是用中英混合数据微调。已有研究在 Whisper 上加小型适配器，中英混说的识别明显变好，但那是研究项目，不是一个设置项。

sections.heading: 换一个为此训练的模型
body: 大量用中文训练的新一代语音模型原生就能处理语言切换。Qwen3-ASR 根本没有语言参数，边听边从声音里判断语言。[TypeAloud 在你的 Mac 上运行 Qwen3-ASR](qwen3-asr-mac)，做成了语音输入应用，中英混着说的句子会按你说的样子写出来。更多见[中英混合语音输入](chinese-english-dictation)。

faq.q: Whisper 支持中文吗？
faq.a: 支持。只说中文时，它的普通话识别不错。问题出在一句话里切换语言。

faq.q: Whisper 为什么输出繁体？
faq.a: 它的训练数据里简体和繁体混在一起。用简体中文写 initial prompt，通常就能让它输出简体。

faq.q: 哪些听写应用用的是 Whisper？
faq.a: 很多 Mac 本地应用都提供 Whisper 模型，包括 [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative)、[VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative) 和 [MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative)。

faq.q: 有能处理中英混说的免费应用吗？
faq.a: TypeAloud 免费开源，在你的 Mac 上本地运行 Qwen3-ASR。

en.title: Offline dictation for Mac — free, no account — TypeAloud
en.description: TypeAloud is free offline dictation for Mac. A speech model runs on your device, so you can dictate into any app without internet, an account or a word limit.
heading: Offline dictation for Mac.
Free, with no account.
en.intro: TypeAloud runs a speech-to-text model on your Mac. Once the model is downloaded you can turn Wi-Fi off and keep dictating into any app, for as long as you like.

sections.heading: How it works without internet
body: On first launch you choose a local model. The recommended one, [Qwen3-ASR 0.6B](qwen3-asr-mac), is a one-time download of about 1 GB. From then on, recording and transcription both happen on your device.
Hold Ctrl+Shift, speak, release. The transcript is inserted where your cursor is. A small prompt with a live waveform shows that TypeAloud is listening.

sections.heading: What stays on your Mac
body: In local mode the audio is processed on your device and transcripts are saved there. Neither is uploaded for transcription. There is no account, so there is no profile on a server tied to what you dictate.

sections.heading: What still uses the network
body: Three things: the first model download, app updates, and the cloud features if you turn them on. Cloud transcription is optional, uses your own Groq or OpenAI key and sends audio to that provider.

sections.heading: What you need
body: A Mac, with Apple Silicon recommended for local dictation. Microphone permission to record, and macOS Accessibility permission so TypeAloud can listen for the shortcut and type into other apps.

faq.q: Does it really work with no connection at all?
faq.a: Yes. After the model download, local dictation needs no network. You can test it by turning Wi-Fi off.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how much I can dictate?
faq.a: No. With a local model there is no monthly bill and no transcription quota.

faq.q: Which languages does it understand?
faq.a: The local Qwen3-ASR model detects the spoken language automatically, including sentences that mix languages.

faq.q: Does it work in every app?
faq.a: It inserts text into the app that has focus. If an app blocks insertion, the finished transcript is still in History for you to copy.

faq.q: What other dictation apps run on a Mac?
faq.a: The [roundup of Mac dictation apps](best-dictation-apps-mac) compares ten of them by price and by whether they transcribe locally or in the cloud.

en.title: Chinese–English mixed dictation for Mac — TypeAloud
en.description: Dictate sentences that mix Chinese and English without switching input languages. TypeAloud transcribes on your Mac with Qwen3-ASR, free and offline.
heading: Speak Chinese and English
in the same sentence.
en.intro: Bilingual people rarely stay in one language. TypeAloud's local model detects what you are speaking as you go, so a sentence that starts in Chinese and ends in English is written down as you said it.

sections.heading: No language switch to remember
body: [Most dictation tools](best-dictation-apps-mac) ask you to pick a language first, then mangle anything outside it. TypeAloud's default local model, Qwen3-ASR, takes no language setting at all. It works out the language from the audio, which is also how it avoids [Whisper's trouble with mixed speech](whisper-chinese-english).
That fits how technical work in Chinese actually sounds: product names, API names and half the nouns are English, and the grammar around them is Chinese.

sections.heading: Built for long dictation
body: Hold Ctrl+Shift for as long as you are talking, then release. Local mode shows progress as text arrives. Completed transcripts go to History, and a failed transcription can be retried when its audio was saved, so a long recording is not lost to one error.

sections.heading: Free, on your device
body: Local transcription needs no account, subscription or API key, and has no word limit. Audio is processed on your Mac. Apple Silicon is recommended.

faq.q: Do I have to set Chinese or English before speaking?
faq.a: No. The local Qwen3-ASR model detects the spoken language automatically.

faq.q: Does it handle English terms inside Chinese sentences?
faq.a: Yes, that is the case it is designed for. Accuracy on unusual names still varies, as with any speech model.

faq.q: Is the interface available in Chinese?
faq.a: Yes. The interface language is a separate setting from the language you speak.

faq.q: Does it work offline?
faq.a: Local transcription works offline after a one-time model download of about 1 GB.

sections.heading: 不用记着切换语言
body: [多数语音输入工具](best-dictation-apps-mac)要你先选一种语言，超出这种语言的部分就识别得乱七八糟。TypeAloud 默认的本地模型 Qwen3-ASR 没有语言设置这一项，它直接从音频里判断语言，这也是它不会像 [Whisper 那样在中英混说时出错](whisper-chinese-english)的原因。
